name: @kitora/theme
description: Kitora's foundations and theming: OKLCH colour scales from one brand colour with contrast-checked foreground pairs, radius / spacing / type / density scales, a ThemeProvider (light, dark, system, per-subtree themes, density), CSS-variable and Tailwind exporters, a live theme designer and a WCAG contrast checker.

exports.name: oklchToRgb
exports.description: OKLCH → gamma sRGB, unclamped (check {@link inGamut} or use {@link toGamut}).

exports.name: rgbToOklch
exports.description: Gamma sRGB → OKLCH. A grey keeps hue 0.

exports.name: inGamut
exports.description: True when every sRGB channel of the colour is displayable.

exports.name: toGamut
exports.description:
The colour brought into sRGB by lowering chroma only (lightness and hue are what a designer picks,
so they stay; CSS Color 4's gamut mapping makes the same choice).

exports.name: luminance
exports.description:
WCAG 2 relative luminance of a colour as a browser paints it on an sRGB screen: out-of-gamut
channels are clipped and rounded to 8 bits, which is what Chrome and Safari do with an `oklch()` too vivid for sRGB (so a
ratio here matches the hex a colour picker reads off the page, and the src/styles.css comments).

exports.name: composite
exports.description: A translucent colour painted over an opaque backdrop, as the eye sees it (composited in sRGB like browsers do).

exports.name: formatOklch
exports.description: CSS `oklch()` text, rounded the way src/styles.css writes it (`oklch(0.47 0.16 162)`, alpha as `/ 35%`).

exports.name: formatHex
exports.description: `#rrggbb` as an sRGB screen shows it (channels clipped, like {@link luminance}); alpha is dropped.

exports.name: parseColor
exports.description: Parses `#rgb`, `#rrggbb(aa)`, `rgb()/rgba()` and `oklch()` text; `null` for anything else.

exports.name: withChannels
exports.description: A copy of `color` with some channels replaced.

exports.name: Oklch
exports.description: A colour in OKLCH. `l` 0–1, `c` ≥ 0 (≈0.37 is the sRGB maximum), `h` degrees 0–360, `alpha` 0–1.

exports.name: Rgb
exports.description: A colour in gamma-encoded sRGB, each channel 0–1 (values outside mean out of gamut).

exports.name: contrastRatio
exports.description: WCAG 2 contrast ratio, 1–21. Translucent foregrounds are composited over the background first.

exports.name: contrastLevel
exports.description: The level a score earns for a use under an algorithm.
exports.signature: (score: number, use?: ContrastUse, algorithm?: ContrastAlgorithm) => ContrastLevel

exports.name: ensureContrast
exports.description:
`fg` with its lightness moved the smallest distance that gives `target` against `bg` (hue and chroma
kept as authored; the ratio is measured as the screen clips it). It goes darker or lighter, whichever side of the background can
reach the target with the smaller change; when neither can, the extreme with the better ratio wins.
exports.signature: (fg: Oklch, bg: Oklch, target: number, algorithm?: ContrastAlgorithm) => Oklch

exports.name: ensureContrastOnTint
exports.description:
`fg` with its lightness moved the smallest distance that gives `target` as text on its OWN tint: `fg` at
`alpha` painted over `under` (a soft button's `bg-destructive/10`, a badge's `/20`). The tint follows the
colour, so this is a separate search from {@link ensureContrast}: it moves away from `under` (darker on a
light surface, lighter on a dark one), snapped outwards to the printed precision. When even the extreme
falls short, the extreme is returned (it is the best there is).
exports.signature: (fg: Oklch, under: Oklch, alpha: number, target: number, algorithm?: ContrastAlgorithm) => Oklch

exports.name: focusRing
exports.description:
A focus-ring colour from a brand colour: the lowest opacity, from `minAlpha` upwards in 5% steps,
whose composite reaches `target` (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 non-text, 3:1 by default) on EVERY backdrop
the ring is drawn over (background, card, muted). When even the opaque colour falls short (a light
amber on white) its lightness is moved with {@link ensureContrast} against the worst backdrop first.
The returned colour carries the alpha, so `ring-ring` (no extra `/NN` opacity) is the full ring.
exports.signature: (color: Oklch, backdrops: readonly Oklch[], minAlpha: number, target?: number, algorithm?: ContrastAlgorithm) => Oklch

exports.name: bestForeground
exports.description: Of `candidates`, the one that reads best on `bg` (e.g. white vs near-black text on a brand fill).
exports.signature: (bg: Oklch, candidates: readonly Oklch[], algorithm?: ContrastAlgorithm) => Oklch

exports.name: auditContrast
exports.description:
Audits `pairs` against a token map (name → colour). Pairs whose tokens are missing or unparsed are
returned in `missing` rather than silently dropped, so a typo in a pair list is visible.
exports.signature: (tokens: ReadonlyMap<string, Oklch>, pairs?: readonly ContrastPair[], algorithm?: ContrastAlgorithm) => { readonly results: readonly ContrastResult[]; readonly missing: readonly ContrastPair[]; }

exports.name: CONTRAST_USES
exports.description: What a foreground/background pair is used for; it decides the minimum ratio.

exports.name: ContrastUse
exports.description: One of {@link CONTRAST_USES}: text, large text or non-text UI.

exports.name: WCAG
exports.description: WCAG 2.2 minimums: SC 1.4.3 (AA text), 1.4.6 (AAA text), 1.4.11 (non-text UI, 3:1).

exports.name: CONTRAST_LEVELS
exports.description: The grade a ratio earns for one use, best first.

exports.name: ContrastLevel
exports.description: One of {@link CONTRAST_LEVELS}: the grade a ratio earns.

exports.name: ContrastAlgorithm
exports.description: The pluggable seam: a function scoring a pair plus what score each use must reach.

exports.name: wcag2
exports.description: The default algorithm: WCAG 2.x ratios.

exports.name: ContrastPair
exports.description: A named pair to audit: token names without the leading `--`.

exports.name: DEFAULT_CONTRAST_PAIRS
exports.description: The pairs every theme in this repo must keep readable (the ones src/styles.css comments argue about).

exports.name: ContrastResult
exports.description: One audited pair.

exports.name: nearestStep
exports.description: The step whose curve lightness is closest to `l`.

exports.name: generateScale
exports.description:
An 11-step ramp from one seed, every step in sRGB gamut. With `anchor` (the default) the seed lands
exactly on its nearest step and the steps around it bend towards it, so the brand colour itself is
in the ramp; without it the ramp follows the curve and only borrows the seed's hue and chroma.
exports.signature: (seed: Oklch, options?: { readonly curve?: ScaleCurve; readonly anchor?: boolean; }) => ColorScale

exports.name: mapSteps
exports.description: Builds a per-step record with every step present (a literal, so the type needs no cast).
exports.signature: <T>(fn: (step: ScaleStep, index: number) => T) => { readonly [S in ScaleStep]: T; }

exports.name: radiusScale
exports.description: Every named radius for a base, in rem.

exports.name: spacingScale
exports.description: Each spacing step in rem for a density.
exports.signature: (density: DensityTokens) => ReadonlyArray<{ readonly step: number; readonly rem: number; }>

exports.name: modularTypeScale
exports.description: A modular type scale: `base` rem at step `base`, multiplied by `ratio` per step (1.125 = major second).
exports.signature: (base: number, ratio: number) => { readonly [S in TypeStep]: number; }

exports.name: SCALE_STEPS
exports.description: Ramp steps, the Tailwind names (`brand-50` … `brand-950`).

exports.name: ScaleStep
exports.description: One ramp step, `50` … `950`.

exports.name: ColorScale
exports.description: One ramp: a colour per step, light to dark.

exports.name: ScaleCurve
exports.description: How a ramp is shaped: a lightness per step and a share of the seed's chroma per step.

exports.name: DEFAULT_SCALE_CURVE
exports.description: A Tailwind-like curve: near-white 50, mid 500, near-black 950.

exports.name: RADIUS_MULTIPLIERS
exports.description: Radius names and their multiple of the base `--radius`, exactly as src/styles.css derives them.

exports.name: RadiusName
exports.description: One named radius, `xs` … `4xl`.

exports.name: DEFAULT_RADIUS
exports.description: The base radius src/styles.css ships, in rem.

exports.name: RADIUS_RANGE
exports.description: The designer's radius range, in rem (0 = square, 1 = very round).

exports.name: DENSITIES
exports.description: The built-in densities. `compact` is the repo's default (Tailwind's 0.25rem spacing unit).

exports.name: DensityName
exports.description: One of {@link DENSITIES}: `compact` or `comfortable`.

exports.name: DensityTokens
exports.description:
What a density sets. `spacing` is Tailwind v4's `--spacing` unit, which every `h-7`, `px-2`, `gap-1`
multiplies, so one variable re-flows every kit component; the rest are named sizes a component can
read directly (`h-(--density-control-h)`).

exports.name: DENSITY_TOKENS
exports.description: Sizes per density, in rem.

exports.name: SPACING_STEPS
exports.description: Tailwind's spacing steps a gallery table shows (multiples of the `--spacing` unit).

exports.name: TYPE_SCALE
exports.description: The type steps src/styles.css defines (`--text-*`), in rem. Tighter than Tailwind's for compact UIs.

exports.name: TypeStep
exports.description: One type step name, `2xs` … `6xl`.

exports.name: TYPE_STEPS
exports.description: The type steps in order, smallest first.

exports.name: buildTheme
exports.description:
Generates a theme. Pure and deterministic: the same config (and overrides) always gives the same tokens.
`overrides` replaces generated tokens per scheme BEFORE the fills are fitted, so a language that paints its
own surfaces (Retro's grey face) still gets a primary and destructive that read on them.

exports.name: brandFrom
exports.description: A brand from colour text (`#10b981`, `oklch(0.6 0.15 162)`); `null` when it does not parse.

exports.name: tokenMap
exports.description: A theme's colour tokens for one scheme as a name → colour map (what {@link auditContrast } reads).

exports.name: pairRatio
exports.description: The contrast of a token pair in a theme, for one-off checks.
exports.signature: (theme: Theme, scheme: Scheme, fg: ColorToken, bg: ColorToken) => number

exports.name: SCHEMES
exports.description: The colour schemes a theme carries.

exports.name: Scheme
exports.description: One of {@link SCHEMES}: `light` or `dark`.

exports.name: COLOR_TOKENS
exports.description: Every colour token a theme sets, by its CSS variable name without `--` (the src/styles.css set).

exports.name: SIDEBAR_TOKENS
exports.description:
The sidebar's tokens (`@kitora/sidebar` reads `--sidebar`, `--sidebar-foreground` and `--sidebar-border`; the rest
keep the shadcn names an app's own sidebar classes use). Each is derived from the theme's own surfaces, so a brand,
a tinted neutral or a language that paints its own surfaces reaches the sidebar; an override sets one directly.

exports.name: SidebarToken
exports.description: One of {@link SIDEBAR_TOKENS}.

exports.name: ColorToken
exports.description: One colour token name, a CSS variable name without `--`.

exports.name: ColorTokens
exports.description: One colour per token: a whole scheme's palette.

exports.name: NeutralTint
exports.description: The neutral greys' tint: src/styles.css uses hue 285 at chroma 0.005 (a cool, barely-there violet).

exports.name: ThemeConfig
exports.description: Everything a theme is generated from.

exports.name: DEFAULT_BRAND
exports.description:
The brand accent, Kitora's cobalt (`#4767D3`, oklch(0.549 0.17 268)), at the light-mode L that clears AA as text on
its own 15% tint over the page, a card, a popup and `muted` (src/styles.css `--primary`, #3A58C3). The brand hex
itself reads 5.06:1 on white but 4.29:1 on that tint over `muted`; the logo keeps the brand hex.

exports.name: DEFAULT_BRAND_DARK
exports.description: The brand accent for dark backgrounds (`#8AA8F7`): dark mode's `primary` (src/styles.css `.dark --primary`).

exports.name: DEFAULT_THEME_CONFIG
exports.description: The config that reproduces src/styles.css.

exports.name: SIDEBAR_MUTED_MIX
exports.description:
How much of `muted` the sidebar's surface carries over the page background: a step off the content, in the theme's
own neutrals (the mix an app wrote by hand before the theme emitted it: `color-mix(in oklab, var(--muted) 55%, var(--background))`).

exports.name: DESTRUCTIVE_SOFT_TINT
exports.description:
The strongest tint of the destructive colour that carries destructive text, per scheme: light mode's
soft button hover (`bg-destructive/15`), dark mode's badge and menu-item highlight (`dark:bg-destructive/20`).
A weaker tint reads better, so passing at these covers every softer one (`/5`, `/8`, `/10`).

exports.name: PRIMARY_SOFT_TINT
exports.description:
The strongest tint of the brand colour that carries primary text, per scheme: the soft button's hover
(`hover:bg-primary/15` in light, `dark:hover:bg-primary/20`). Passing here covers its rest state (`/10`, `/15`)
and every softer tint (a selected chip, a 10% badge).

exports.name: ThemeAdjustment
exports.description: One contrast fix the generator made, for the designer's report.

exports.name: Theme
exports.description: A generated theme.

exports.name: ThemeOverrides
exports.description:
Tokens a theme is built around, per scheme. A surface or text token (background, card, muted…) is used as
given, and the fills are fitted against it; a fill (`primary`, `destructive`) is that fill's seed, fitted
like the config's. The labels and the ring are taken as given (they are not re-checked).

exports.name: foundationVariables
exports.description: The non-colour variables (radius base, spacing unit, density sizes) a scheme-independent block carries.

exports.name: brandVariables
exports.description: The brand ramp as `brand-50` … `brand-950` variables.

exports.name: colorVariables
exports.description: One scheme's colour variables.

exports.name: schemeVariables
exports.description: Every variable of one scheme, foundations first (what an inline `style` or a scoped block needs).

exports.name: toCss
exports.description:
The theme as plain CSS: foundations, the brand ramp and light colours on `selectors.light`, dark
colours on `selectors.dark`. With `only` set, a single scheme's full set goes on `selectors.light`
(a subtree pinned to one scheme).
exports.signature: (theme: Theme, selectors?: CssSelectors, only?: Scheme) => string

exports.name: toTailwindV4
exports.description:
A Tailwind v4 stylesheet with Kitora's default look: the CSS variables, an `@theme inline` block wiring them (and the
fonts, tracking, shadows, status and chart colours and motion of {@link KITORA_FOUNDATIONS}) to utilities, the Geist fallback
faces and the base rules. It starts with `@import "tailwindcss"`; the host loads Geist itself.

exports.name: toTailwindV3
exports.description: A Tailwind v3 `tailwind.config.js`: colours and radii point at the CSS variables (ship {@link toCss} beside it).

exports.name: toTokensJson
exports.description: Design-token JSON (W3C DTCG shape: `$value` / `$type`), both schemes plus foundations, with hex fallbacks.

exports.name: ThemeExporter
exports.description: The pluggable seam: one export format.

exports.name: CssSelectors
exports.description: Where scheme blocks go: `:root` + `.dark` by default (the class src/styles.css switches on).

exports.name: DEFAULT_SELECTORS
exports.description: Kitora's selectors: `:root` for light and `.dark` for dark.

exports.name: KITORA_FOUNDATIONS
exports.description:
The rest of Kitora's default look, beyond the generated colours, radius and type scale: the values the Kitora site's
own stylesheet (src/styles.css) defines, so an app built from {@link toTailwindV4} looks like the site by default.
src/__tests__/site-theme-export.test.ts fails when the site and these drift apart.

exports.name: GEIST_FALLBACK_FACES
exports.description:
Geist's metrics on Arial (Liberation Sans where Arial is missing) and Geist Mono's on Courier New: the faces text
shows until Geist arrives, measured so the swap keeps line breaks and heights (the site's own fallback faces).

exports.name: TAILWIND_V4_BASE
exports.description:
The base rules the components' classes and the site's look rely on: a bare `border`, `border-t` or `outline` takes
the theme's border and (half-strength) ring colour (Tailwind v4's own default is `currentColor`, which drew a dialog
footer's rule in the text colour); the page's font, colours and colour scheme; the selection colour; the hand cursor
on controls (Tailwind v4 sets buttons to the default arrow); the keyboard focus ring. The same rules as the site's.

exports.name: DEFAULT_EXPORTERS
exports.description: The built-in formats, in the order the designer's Export tabs show them.

exports.name: BrandPreset
exports.description: A named brand colour the designer offers as a one-click starting point.

exports.name: BRAND_PRESETS
exports.description: The built-in brand presets, at their light-mode lightness (the gallery Theme Lab's set).

exports.name: isDirection
exports.description: Whether `value` is a {@link Direction}; use it to read an untrusted attribute or stored choice.

exports.name: resolveDirection
exports.description:
The first candidate that is a direction, compared case-insensitively
(attributes are written `RTL` too); anything else, `auto` included, is
skipped; none at all gives `ltr`. Pass the most specific source first:
`resolveDirection(props.dir, element.dir, documentDir)`.

exports.name: flipDirection
exports.description: The other direction.

exports.name: directionForLocale
exports.description: The direction a BCP 47 locale is written in: `ar-EG` → rtl, `en-US` → ltr, `az-Arab` → rtl.

exports.name: DIRECTIONS
exports.description: The resolved reading directions (`auto` is resolved by the browser, never stored).

exports.name: Direction
exports.description: A resolved reading direction: `ltr` or `rtl`.

exports.name: DEFAULT_DIRECTION
exports.description: Used when nothing says otherwise: HTML's own default.

exports.name: RTL_LANGUAGES
exports.description:
Primary language subtags written right to left (Arabic, Aramaic, Dhivehi,
Persian, Hebrew and its old `iw` code, N'Ko, Pashto, Sindhi, Syriac, Uyghur,
Urdu, Yiddish, Sorani Kurdish). A script subtag overrides it either way
(`az-Arab` is rtl, `ku-Latn` is ltr), see {@link directionForLocale}.

exports.name: RTL_SCRIPTS
exports.description: Script subtags written right to left.

exports.name: validateLanguage
exports.description:
Every problem with a value that claims to be a {@link DesignLanguage}; empty when it is one. Checks
the id shape, every slot field (present and in range) and token references. For data from outside
the type system: a theme imported from a file, read back from browser storage, or posted by a user.

exports.name: slotFields
exports.description: The slot field names per slot, from {@link SLOT_SCHEMA} (what the guard test compares adapters against).

exports.name: slotFieldSpecs
exports.description: Each field of a slot with its spec, in schema order (what an editor draws a form from).

exports.name: createLanguageRegistry
exports.description: Creates a registry holding `initial` (and offering `options.loaders`); every language is validated on register, and an invalid one throws.

exports.name: Px
exports.description: A length in CSS pixels (a renderer converts: points on native, cells in a terminal).

exports.name: FixedCorner
exports.description:
A corner radius of its own: a step of the theme's radius scale (so it follows the theme's base radius, as the
Kitora look does), a multiple of that base radius between the steps (`{ scale: 1.25 }`, Kitora's
square avatar), or a fixed size (macOS controls keep their radius whatever the theme says).

exports.name: CORNER_ROLES
exports.description: The shared corners a slot may name instead of a value of its own: every input-like control and button, or every card, popover, menu and dialog.

exports.name: CornerRole
exports.description: One of {@link CORNER_ROLES}.

exports.name: Corner
exports.description:
A corner radius: a {@link FixedCorner}, or a shared role (`{ role: "control" }`) whose value the language's base slot holds
(`base.control`, `base.surface`), so one change there moves every slot that names it. Kitora's controls and surfaces name
their role; a language that really differs (macOS, Material, Retro) gives a slot a value of its own.

exports.name: Paint
exports.description: A colour, always a reference to a theme token (optionally see-through), never a raw colour value.

exports.name: Fill
exports.description: A paint, or nothing painted (transparent).

exports.name: PerScheme
exports.description: A value that differs between light and dark (a field fill that is white in light, tinted in dark).

exports.name: CONTROL_SIZES
exports.description: The control sizes a button comes in, smallest first (the `size` prop's `xs` … `xl`; `md` is `default`).

exports.name: ControlSize
exports.description: One of a button's sizes, `xs` to `xl` (`md` is the `default` size).

exports.name: PerSize
exports.description: One value per button size, keyed `xs` … `xl`.

exports.name: SWITCH_SIZES
exports.description: The sizes a switch comes in (the `size` prop: `sm`, `default`, and the opt-in `lg`).

exports.name: SwitchSize
exports.description: One of a switch's sizes: `sm`, `default` or `lg`.

exports.name: SWITCH_BORDER
exports.description:
The switch track's border on each side, in CSS pixels: the track is drawn with a 1px border (transparent
unless the language gives an `edge`), so the thumb slides inside `width - 2 * SWITCH_BORDER`. A renderer
with a different border width must say so; {@link validateLanguage} checks the thumb against this.

exports.name: PerSwitchSize
exports.description: One value per switch size, keyed `sm`, `default`, `lg`.

exports.name: SELECT_SIZES
exports.description: The sizes a select trigger comes in (the `size` prop: `sm`, `default` and the opt-in `lg`); a native select is the `sm` size, or `default`.

exports.name: SelectSize
exports.description: One of a select trigger's sizes: `sm`, `default` or `lg`.

exports.name: PerSelectSize
exports.description: One value per select size, keyed `sm`, `default`, `lg`.

exports.name: TOGGLE_SIZES
exports.description: The three sizes a toggle comes in (the `size` prop: `sm`, `default`, `lg`).

exports.name: ToggleSize
exports.description: One of a toggle's sizes: `sm`, `default` or `lg`.

exports.name: PerToggleSize
exports.description: One value per toggle size, keyed `sm`, `default`, `lg`.

exports.name: BUTTON_FILLS
exports.description: How a solid button is filled: one flat colour, or a soft top-to-bottom sheen (macOS push buttons).

exports.name: ELEVATIONS
exports.description: How much a control lifts off the page: a hairline shadow, a visible raised edge, or a classic 3D bevel (light top-left, dark bottom-right; fields and small controls sunken).

exports.name: PRESS_STYLES
exports.description: What pressing a button does: nudge it down 1px (Kitora), or sink it with an inner shadow (macOS).

exports.name: FOCUS_RINGS
exports.description:
The keyboard-focus indicator: a solid ring (Kitora), a wider, softer halo (macOS), or an accent stroke along the
bottom of a field with no ring (Windows 11). On a toggle (checkbox, radio, switch, slider, toggle) `underline` draws as
`solid`: a stroke under a small control is not a focus indicator.

exports.name: BEVELS
exports.description: A field's edge: flat, a faint inner top shadow that makes it read as recessed (macOS), or the classic sunken bevel (Retro).

exports.name: TABS_STYLES
exports.description: How a tab list draws the selected tab: a raised segment in a track, or a line under it.

exports.name: SURFACES
exports.description: A menu's surface: opaque, or see-through with the page blurred behind it (macOS).

exports.name: HIGHLIGHTS
exports.description: Which colour a highlighted menu item takes: the quiet accent, or the brand colour (macOS).

exports.name: CHECKMARK_SIDES
exports.description: Which side a menu's checkmark sits on.

exports.name: PRESENTATIONS
exports.description: Where a dialog appears: centred, or dropped from the top edge like a macOS sheet.

exports.name: FOOTER_STYLES
exports.description: A dialog footer: a tinted band with a top rule (Kitora), or plain (macOS).

exports.name: MOTION_STYLES
exports.description:
How popups and dialogs move: Kitora's quick fade and zoom (`subtle`), no entrance or exit movement (`none`), or a slower
entrance that overshoots a little (`spring`; sliding panels and toasts only take a little longer, without the overshoot). A dialog presented as a sheet slides from the top edge (unless `none`) and eases
out without overshoot. `prefers-reduced-motion` turns these animations off in every language.

exports.name: FONT_FAMILIES
exports.description: Which font family the language sets: the theme's brand face, the OS's own, Windows' own (Segoe UI Variable first), or a monospace.

exports.name: TOOLTIP_STYLES
exports.description: A tooltip's colours: inverted (the foreground colour with page-coloured text, Kitora), or a small popover-coloured panel with a hairline edge (macOS).

exports.name: SEGMENT_STYLES
exports.description:
A joined toggle group (no spacing between its items): items butted together with only the ends rounded (Kitora),
or a segmented control, a filled track with every segment rounded inside it (macOS).

exports.name: BAR_ENDS
exports.description: How the ends of a progress or meter bar are drawn: rounded (Kitora), or square (Retro, Terminal).

exports.name: BAR_HIGHLIGHTS
exports.description: What a menu bar title takes under the pointer or while its menu is open: the quiet muted fill (Kitora), the accent, or the brand colour with its foreground (Retro).

exports.name: TOOLBAR_PRESSED_STYLES
exports.description: A pressed toolbar button: a brand tint with brand text (Kitora), a muted fill, or pressed into the classic sunken bevel (Retro).

exports.name: AVATAR_SHAPES
exports.description: An avatar's outline: a circle (Kitora), a rounded square that scales with the avatar (a quarter of its side), or a square (Retro).

exports.name: CALENDAR_SELECTED_SHAPES
exports.description: A selected calendar day's outline: a circle (macOS, Material), a square (Retro, Terminal), or rounded by the slot's `cellCorner` (Kitora).

exports.name: CALENDAR_TODAY_STYLES
exports.description:
How a calendar marks today: a ring in the selected colour (Material), a dot under the number, a bolder number in the text colour, or the
number in the brand colour, semibold (`accent`, Kitora). A selected today takes the selected fill and keeps only its dot.

exports.name: CALENDAR_RANGE_BANDS
exports.description:
How the days inside a range are joined: one band across the row with the ends cornered by `cellCorner` (Kitora), a band with fully
round ends (a pill, macOS and Material), or no band at all, each day tinted on its own shape (Retro, Terminal).

exports.name: CALENDAR_WEEKDAY_CASES
exports.description: The weekday header's letters: as the locale writes them (`title`, "Mo Tu"), or in capitals ("MO TU").

exports.name: CALENDAR_HEADERS
exports.description: The caption row: the month centred between the arrows (Kitora), or at the start with both arrows grouped at the end (macOS, Material).

exports.name: SHADOW_SCALES
exports.description:
The shadow scale every part without a slot of its own wears (Tailwind's `shadow-xs` … `shadow-2xl`, which a host routes through
`--dk-base-shadow-*`): the page's own scale (`host`, Kitora), a hairline edge under a soft drop (`crisp`: macOS, Windows 11,
GNOME), Material's key-plus-ambient elevation levels (`tonal`), the classic 3D bevel, framed from `md` up (`bevel`: Retro), or no
shadow at all (`flat`: Terminal).

exports.name: KIT_FOLLOWS

Where a language's colours come from.

- `generated`: a theme built by {@link buildTheme } from a seed (so every text pair is contrast-checked),

exports.description:
Every field each slot must carry, with its check. This table IS the slot schema at runtime: a
language read from JSON (an imported or browser-saved theme) is checked against it before use, and the
guard test checks every registered language with it. `satisfies` ties it to the TypeScript types, so a
field added to a slot interface without a check here fails to compile.

exports.name: LanguageChoice
exports.description: A language on offer, by id and label: enough for a picker to list it before its data has loaded.

exports.name: LanguageLoader
exports.description: Loads a language's data (typically a dynamic `import()` of its module).

exports.name: LanguageLoaderEntry
exports.description: A language offered through a loader: its id and label up front, its data when {@link LanguageRegistry.load} asks.

exports.name: LanguageRegistry
exports.description:
The languages an app offers. Built-ins and an app's own register the same way; the first registered
one is the default unless `defaultId` says otherwise. A language is offered with its data (`register`)
or through a loader (`registerLoader`): the synchronous reads (`get`, `list`, `fallback`, `resolve`) see
the languages whose data is in, and `load` brings a lazily offered one in. A registry is a plain object
with no hidden state outside it, so two providers (or a test) never share one by accident; a provider
re-reads it when it changes (`subscribe`).

exports.name: LanguageRegistryOptions
exports.description: Options for {@link createLanguageRegistry}.

exports.name: builtinLanguageRegistry
exports.description:
A fresh registry offering the built-ins (Kitora the default): Kitora's data is in it, the six others register
through their loaders and load on `registry.load(id)` (a provider calls it when one is chosen). Register an app's own
on it. For a registry with every built-in's data up front: `createLanguageRegistry(BUILTIN_LANGUAGES)`.

exports.name: tryCompleteLanguage
exports.description:
A language saved before a slot (or a slot field) existed, made whole: every missing slot and every
missing slot field comes from `base` (default Kitora, so a missing field looks as Kitora's does),
as does a size missing from a per-size field (a switch saved before the `lg` size gets the base's `lg`;
each size is checked on its own, so the base's size fits whatever the language's other sizes are),
and the result is validated strictly, so a field that is present but wrong still fails. For languages
from outside the type system (a saved or imported theme, an older release): the adapter and the React
scope use it, so a language written before this batch of slots renders instead of crashing. The
registry stays strict (`register` rejects an incomplete language); complete first when you want it kept.

exports.name: completeLanguage
exports.description: {@link tryCompleteLanguage}, throwing every problem (as `register` does) when the language cannot be made valid.

keeps the default pixel-identical. Change one only together with the component's fallback.

exports.name: BUILTIN_LANGUAGE_LOADERS

language below it.

exports.name: LanguageScope
exports.description:
A subtree in another language, beside the page's own (a side-by-side comparison, a preview). In the
provider's active language it reuses the provider's stylesheet; alone, or in any other language, it
installs its own. Anchored popups opened inside the scope (menus, popovers, tooltips, preview cards, selects,
comboboxes, anchored toasts) portal into a host element at the end of the scope, so they keep its language (variables and
slots) with no `container` prop on any of them. Fixed popups (dialogs, alert dialogs, sheets, drawers) stay in the body,
because a scope or its ancestors may be transformed, scaled or clipped (`DrawerIndent` does all three) and `position: fixed`
would then be laid out against that box; they carry the scope's `data-language` (and a `dark` or `light` class from its
`className`) on their portal node instead, so the same variables resolve. A part's own `container` still wins, and a scope
nested in another picks the nearest. The host takes no layout box and is the scope's last child (use `gap`, not `space-y-*`,
on the scope's `className`). The scope and its ancestors are their owner's: a positioned scope with `overflow: hidden`
clips the popups that open inside it, as any such box would.

exports.description:
`fg` with its lightness moved the smallest distance that gives `target` against `bg` (hue and chroma
kept as authored; the ratio is measured as the screen clips it). It goes darker or lighter, whichever side of the background can
reach the target with the smaller change; when neither can, the extreme with the better ratio wins.

exports.name: ensureContrastOnTint
exports.description:
`fg` with its lightness moved the smallest distance that gives `target` as text on its OWN tint: `fg` at
`alpha` painted over `under` (a soft button's `bg-destructive/10`, a badge's `/20`). The tint follows the
colour, so this is a separate search from {@link ensureContrast}: it moves away from `under` (darker on a
light surface, lighter on a dark one), snapped outwards to the printed precision. When even the extreme
falls short, the extreme is returned (it is the best there is).
exports.signature: (fg: Oklch, under: Oklch, alpha: number, target: number, algorithm?: ContrastAlgorithm) => Oklch

exports.name: focusRing
exports.description:
A focus-ring colour from a brand colour: the lowest opacity, from `minAlpha` upwards in 5% steps,
whose composite reaches `target` (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 non-text, 3:1 by default) on EVERY backdrop
the ring is drawn over (background, card, muted). When even the opaque colour falls short (a light
amber on white) its lightness is moved with {@link ensureContrast} against the worst backdrop first.
The returned colour carries the alpha, so `ring-ring` (no extra `/NN` opacity) is the full ring.
exports.signature: (color: Oklch, backdrops: readonly Oklch[], minAlpha: number, target?: number, algorithm?: ContrastAlgorithm) => Oklch

exports.name: bestForeground
exports.description: Of `candidates`, the one that reads best on `bg` (e.g. white vs near-black text on a brand fill).
exports.signature: (bg: Oklch, candidates: readonly Oklch[], algorithm?: ContrastAlgorithm) => Oklch

exports.name: auditContrast
exports.description:
Audits `pairs` against a token map (name → colour). Pairs whose tokens are missing or unparsed are
returned in `missing` rather than silently dropped, so a typo in a pair list is visible.
exports.signature: (tokens: ReadonlyMap<string, Oklch>, pairs?: readonly ContrastPair[], algorithm?: ContrastAlgorithm) => { readonly results: readonly ContrastResult[]; readonly missing: readonly ContrastPair[]; }

exports.name: CONTRAST_USES
exports.description: What a foreground/background pair is used for; it decides the minimum ratio.

exports.name: ContrastUse
exports.description: One of {@link CONTRAST_USES}: text, large text or non-text UI.

exports.name: WCAG
exports.description: WCAG 2.2 minimums: SC 1.4.3 (AA text), 1.4.6 (AAA text), 1.4.11 (non-text UI, 3:1).

exports.name: CONTRAST_LEVELS
exports.description: The grade a ratio earns for one use, best first.

exports.name: ContrastLevel
exports.description: One of {@link CONTRAST_LEVELS}: the grade a ratio earns.

exports.name: ContrastAlgorithm
exports.description: The pluggable seam: a function scoring a pair plus what score each use must reach.

exports.name: wcag2
exports.description: The default algorithm: WCAG 2.x ratios.

exports.name: ContrastPair
exports.description: A named pair to audit: token names without the leading `--`.

exports.name: DEFAULT_CONTRAST_PAIRS
exports.description: The pairs every theme in this repo must keep readable (the ones src/styles.css comments argue about).

exports.name: ContrastResult
exports.description: One audited pair.

exports.name: nearestStep
exports.description: The step whose curve lightness is closest to `l`.

exports.name: generateScale
exports.description:
An 11-step ramp from one seed, every step in sRGB gamut. With `anchor` (the default) the seed lands
exactly on its nearest step and the steps around it bend towards it, so the brand colour itself is
in the ramp; without it the ramp follows the curve and only borrows the seed's hue and chroma.
exports.signature: (seed: Oklch, options?: { readonly curve?: ScaleCurve; readonly anchor?: boolean; }) => ColorScale

exports.name: mapSteps
exports.description: Builds a per-step record with every step present (a literal, so the type needs no cast).
exports.signature: <T>(fn: (step: ScaleStep, index: number) => T) => { readonly [S in ScaleStep]: T; }

exports.name: radiusScale
exports.description: Every named radius for a base, in rem.

exports.name: spacingScale
exports.description: Each spacing step in rem for a density.
exports.signature: (density: DensityTokens) => ReadonlyArray<{ readonly step: number; readonly rem: number; }>

exports.name: modularTypeScale
exports.description: A modular type scale: `base` rem at step `base`, multiplied by `ratio` per step (1.125 = major second).
exports.signature: (base: number, ratio: number) => { readonly [S in TypeStep]: number; }

exports.name: SCALE_STEPS
exports.description: Ramp steps, the Tailwind names (`brand-50` … `brand-950`).

exports.name: ScaleStep
exports.description: One ramp step, `50` … `950`.

exports.name: ColorScale
exports.description: One ramp: a colour per step, light to dark.

exports.name: ScaleCurve
exports.description: How a ramp is shaped: a lightness per step and a share of the seed's chroma per step.

exports.name: DEFAULT_SCALE_CURVE
exports.description: A Tailwind-like curve: near-white 50, mid 500, near-black 950.

exports.name: RADIUS_MULTIPLIERS
exports.description: Radius names and their multiple of the base `--radius`, exactly as src/styles.css derives them.

exports.name: RadiusName
exports.description: One named radius, `xs` … `4xl`.

exports.name: DEFAULT_RADIUS
exports.description: The base radius src/styles.css ships, in rem.

exports.name: RADIUS_RANGE
exports.description: The designer's radius range, in rem (0 = square, 1 = very round).

exports.name: DENSITIES
exports.description: The built-in densities. `compact` is the repo's default (Tailwind's 0.25rem spacing unit).

exports.name: DensityName
exports.description: One of {@link DENSITIES}: `compact` or `comfortable`.

exports.name: DensityTokens
exports.description:
What a density sets. `spacing` is Tailwind v4's `--spacing` unit, which every `h-7`, `px-2`, `gap-1`
multiplies, so one variable re-flows every kit component; the rest are named sizes a component can
read directly (`h-(--density-control-h)`).

exports.name: DENSITY_TOKENS
exports.description: Sizes per density, in rem.

exports.name: SPACING_STEPS
exports.description: Tailwind's spacing steps a gallery table shows (multiples of the `--spacing` unit).

exports.name: TYPE_SCALE
exports.description: The type steps src/styles.css defines (`--text-*`), in rem. Tighter than Tailwind's for compact UIs.

exports.name: TypeStep
exports.description: One type step name, `2xs` … `6xl`.

exports.name: TYPE_STEPS
exports.description: The type steps in order, smallest first.

exports.name: buildTheme
exports.description:
Generates a theme. Pure and deterministic: the same config (and overrides) always gives the same tokens.
`overrides` replaces generated tokens per scheme BEFORE the fills are fitted, so a language that paints its
own surfaces (Retro's grey face) still gets a primary and destructive that read on them.

exports.name: brandFrom
exports.description: A brand from colour text (`#10b981`, `oklch(0.6 0.15 162)`); `null` when it does not parse.

exports.name: tokenMap
exports.description: A theme's colour tokens for one scheme as a name → colour map (what {@link auditContrast } reads).

exports.name: pairRatio
exports.description: The contrast of a token pair in a theme, for one-off checks.
exports.signature: (theme: Theme, scheme: Scheme, fg: ColorToken, bg: ColorToken) => number

exports.name: SCHEMES
exports.description: The colour schemes a theme carries.

exports.name: Scheme
exports.description: One of {@link SCHEMES}: `light` or `dark`.

exports.name: COLOR_TOKENS
exports.description: Every colour token a theme sets, by its CSS variable name without `--` (the src/styles.css set).

exports.name: SIDEBAR_TOKENS
exports.description:
The sidebar's tokens (`@kitora/sidebar` reads `--sidebar`, `--sidebar-foreground` and `--sidebar-border`; the rest
keep the shadcn names an app's own sidebar classes use). Each is derived from the theme's own surfaces, so a brand,
a tinted neutral or a language that paints its own surfaces reaches the sidebar; an override sets one directly.

exports.name: SidebarToken
exports.description: One of {@link SIDEBAR_TOKENS}.

exports.name: ColorToken
exports.description: One colour token name, a CSS variable name without `--`.

exports.name: ColorTokens
exports.description: One colour per token: a whole scheme's palette.

exports.name: NeutralTint
exports.description: The neutral greys' tint: src/styles.css uses hue 285 at chroma 0.005 (a cool, barely-there violet).

exports.name: ThemeConfig
exports.description: Everything a theme is generated from.

exports.name: DEFAULT_BRAND
exports.description:
The brand accent, Kitora's cobalt (`#4767D3`, oklch(0.549 0.17 268)), at the light-mode L that clears AA as text on
its own 15% tint over the page, a card, a popup and `muted` (src/styles.css `--primary`, #3A58C3). The brand hex
itself reads 5.06:1 on white but 4.29:1 on that tint over `muted`; the logo keeps the brand hex.

exports.name: DEFAULT_BRAND_DARK
exports.description: The brand accent for dark backgrounds (`#8AA8F7`): dark mode's `primary` (src/styles.css `.dark --primary`).

exports.name: DEFAULT_THEME_CONFIG
exports.description: The config that reproduces src/styles.css.

exports.name: SIDEBAR_MUTED_MIX
exports.description:
How much of `muted` the sidebar's surface carries over the page background: a step off the content, in the theme's
own neutrals (the mix an app wrote by hand before the theme emitted it: `color-mix(in oklab, var(--muted) 55%, var(--background))`).

exports.name: DESTRUCTIVE_SOFT_TINT
exports.description:
The strongest tint of the destructive colour that carries destructive text, per scheme: light mode's
soft button hover (`bg-destructive/15`), dark mode's badge and menu-item highlight (`dark:bg-destructive/20`).
A weaker tint reads better, so passing at these covers every softer one (`/5`, `/8`, `/10`).

exports.name: PRIMARY_SOFT_TINT
exports.description:
The strongest tint of the brand colour that carries primary text, per scheme: the soft button's hover
(`hover:bg-primary/15` in light, `dark:hover:bg-primary/20`). Passing here covers its rest state (`/10`, `/15`)
and every softer tint (a selected chip, a 10% badge).

exports.name: ThemeAdjustment
exports.description: One contrast fix the generator made, for the designer's report.

exports.name: Theme
exports.description: A generated theme.

exports.name: ThemeOverrides
exports.description:
Tokens a theme is built around, per scheme. A surface or text token (background, card, muted…) is used as
given, and the fills are fitted against it; a fill (`primary`, `destructive`) is that fill's seed, fitted
like the config's. The labels and the ring are taken as given (they are not re-checked).

exports.name: foundationVariables
exports.description: The non-colour variables (radius base, spacing unit, density sizes) a scheme-independent block carries.

exports.name: brandVariables
exports.description: The brand ramp as `brand-50` … `brand-950` variables.

exports.name: colorVariables
exports.description: One scheme's colour variables.

exports.name: schemeVariables
exports.description: Every variable of one scheme, foundations first (what an inline `style` or a scoped block needs).

exports.name: toCss
exports.description:
The theme as plain CSS: foundations, the brand ramp and light colours on `selectors.light`, dark
colours on `selectors.dark`. With `only` set, a single scheme's full set goes on `selectors.light`
(a subtree pinned to one scheme).
exports.signature: (theme: Theme, selectors?: CssSelectors, only?: Scheme) => string

exports.name: toTailwindV4
exports.description:
A Tailwind v4 stylesheet with Kitora's default look: the CSS variables, an `@theme inline` block wiring them (and the
fonts, tracking, shadows, status and chart colours and motion of {@link KITORA_FOUNDATIONS}) to utilities, the Geist fallback
faces and the base rules. It starts with `@import "tailwindcss"`; the host loads Geist itself.

exports.name: toTailwindV3
exports.description: A Tailwind v3 `tailwind.config.js`: colours and radii point at the CSS variables (ship {@link toCss} beside it).

exports.name: toTokensJson
exports.description: Design-token JSON (W3C DTCG shape: `$value` / `$type`), both schemes plus foundations, with hex fallbacks.

exports.name: ThemeExporter
exports.description: The pluggable seam: one export format.

exports.name: CssSelectors
exports.description: Where scheme blocks go: `:root` + `.dark` by default (the class src/styles.css switches on).

exports.name: DEFAULT_SELECTORS
exports.description: Kitora's selectors: `:root` for light and `.dark` for dark.

exports.name: KITORA_FOUNDATIONS
exports.description:
The rest of Kitora's default look, beyond the generated colours, radius and type scale: the values the Kitora site's
own stylesheet (src/styles.css) defines, so an app built from {@link toTailwindV4} looks like the site by default.
src/__tests__/site-theme-export.test.ts fails when the site and these drift apart.

exports.name: GEIST_FALLBACK_FACES
exports.description:
Geist's metrics on Arial (Liberation Sans where Arial is missing) and Geist Mono's on Courier New: the faces text
shows until Geist arrives, measured so the swap keeps line breaks and heights (the site's own fallback faces).

exports.name: TAILWIND_V4_BASE
exports.description:
The base rules the components' classes and the site's look rely on: a bare `border`, `border-t` or `outline` takes
the theme's border and (half-strength) ring colour (Tailwind v4's own default is `currentColor`, which drew a dialog
footer's rule in the text colour); the page's font, colours and colour scheme; the selection colour; the hand cursor
on controls (Tailwind v4 sets buttons to the default arrow); the keyboard focus ring. The same rules as the site's.

exports.name: DEFAULT_EXPORTERS
exports.description: The built-in formats, in the order the designer's Export tabs show them.

exports.name: BrandPreset
exports.description: A named brand colour the designer offers as a one-click starting point.

exports.name: BRAND_PRESETS
exports.description: The built-in brand presets, at their light-mode lightness (the gallery Theme Lab's set).

exports.name: isDirection
exports.description: Whether `value` is a {@link Direction}; use it to read an untrusted attribute or stored choice.

exports.name: resolveDirection
exports.description:
The first candidate that is a direction, compared case-insensitively
(attributes are written `RTL` too); anything else, `auto` included, is
skipped; none at all gives `ltr`. Pass the most specific source first:
`resolveDirection(props.dir, element.dir, documentDir)`.

exports.name: flipDirection
exports.description: The other direction.

exports.name: directionForLocale
exports.description: The direction a BCP 47 locale is written in: `ar-EG` → rtl, `en-US` → ltr, `az-Arab` → rtl.

exports.name: DIRECTIONS
exports.description: The resolved reading directions (`auto` is resolved by the browser, never stored).

exports.name: Direction
exports.description: A resolved reading direction: `ltr` or `rtl`.

exports.name: DEFAULT_DIRECTION
exports.description: Used when nothing says otherwise: HTML's own default.

exports.name: RTL_LANGUAGES
exports.description:
Primary language subtags written right to left (Arabic, Aramaic, Dhivehi,
Persian, Hebrew and its old `iw` code, N'Ko, Pashto, Sindhi, Syriac, Uyghur,
Urdu, Yiddish, Sorani Kurdish). A script subtag overrides it either way
(`az-Arab` is rtl, `ku-Latn` is ltr), see {@link directionForLocale}.

exports.name: RTL_SCRIPTS
exports.description: Script subtags written right to left.

exports.name: validateLanguage
exports.description:
Every problem with a value that claims to be a {@link DesignLanguage}; empty when it is one. Checks
the id shape, every slot field (present and in range) and token references. For data from outside
the type system: a theme imported from a file, read back from browser storage, or posted by a user.

exports.name: slotFields
exports.description: The slot field names per slot, from {@link SLOT_SCHEMA} (what the guard test compares adapters against).

exports.name: slotFieldSpecs
exports.description: Each field of a slot with its spec, in schema order (what an editor draws a form from).

exports.name: createLanguageRegistry
exports.description: Creates a registry holding `initial` (and offering `options.loaders`); every language is validated on register, and an invalid one throws.

exports.name: Px
exports.description: A length in CSS pixels (a renderer converts: points on native, cells in a terminal).

exports.name: FixedCorner
exports.description:
A corner radius of its own: a step of the theme's radius scale (so it follows the theme's base radius, as the
Kitora look does), a multiple of that base radius between the steps (`{ scale: 1.25 }`, Kitora's
square avatar), or a fixed size (macOS controls keep their radius whatever the theme says).

exports.name: CORNER_ROLES
exports.description: The shared corners a slot may name instead of a value of its own: every input-like control and button, or every card, popover, menu and dialog.

exports.name: CornerRole
exports.description: One of {@link CORNER_ROLES}.

exports.name: Corner
exports.description:
A corner radius: a {@link FixedCorner}, or a shared role (`{ role: "control" }`) whose value the language's base slot holds
(`base.control`, `base.surface`), so one change there moves every slot that names it. Kitora's controls and surfaces name
their role; a language that really differs (macOS, Material, Retro) gives a slot a value of its own.

exports.name: Paint
exports.description: A colour, always a reference to a theme token (optionally see-through), never a raw colour value.

exports.name: Fill
exports.description: A paint, or nothing painted (transparent).

exports.name: PerScheme
exports.description: A value that differs between light and dark (a field fill that is white in light, tinted in dark).

exports.name: CONTROL_SIZES
exports.description: The control sizes a button comes in, smallest first (the `size` prop's `xs` … `xl`; `md` is `default`).

exports.name: ControlSize
exports.description: One of a button's sizes, `xs` to `xl` (`md` is the `default` size).

exports.name: PerSize
exports.description: One value per button size, keyed `xs` … `xl`.

exports.name: SWITCH_SIZES
exports.description: The sizes a switch comes in (the `size` prop: `sm`, `default`, and the opt-in `lg`).

exports.name: SwitchSize
exports.description: One of a switch's sizes: `sm`, `default` or `lg`.

exports.name: SWITCH_BORDER
exports.description:
The switch track's border on each side, in CSS pixels: the track is drawn with a 1px border (transparent
unless the language gives an `edge`), so the thumb slides inside `width - 2 * SWITCH_BORDER`. A renderer
with a different border width must say so; {@link validateLanguage} checks the thumb against this.

exports.name: PerSwitchSize
exports.description: One value per switch size, keyed `sm`, `default`, `lg`.

exports.name: SELECT_SIZES
exports.description: The sizes a select trigger comes in (the `size` prop: `sm`, `default` and the opt-in `lg`); a native select is the `sm` size, or `default`.

exports.name: SelectSize
exports.description: One of a select trigger's sizes: `sm`, `default` or `lg`.

exports.name: PerSelectSize
exports.description: One value per select size, keyed `sm`, `default`, `lg`.

exports.name: TOGGLE_SIZES
exports.description: The three sizes a toggle comes in (the `size` prop: `sm`, `default`, `lg`).

exports.name: ToggleSize
exports.description: One of a toggle's sizes: `sm`, `default` or `lg`.

exports.name: PerToggleSize
exports.description: One value per toggle size, keyed `sm`, `default`, `lg`.

exports.name: BUTTON_FILLS
exports.description: How a solid button is filled: one flat colour, or a soft top-to-bottom sheen (macOS push buttons).

exports.name: ELEVATIONS
exports.description: How much a control lifts off the page: a hairline shadow, a visible raised edge, or a classic 3D bevel (light top-left, dark bottom-right; fields and small controls sunken).

exports.name: PRESS_STYLES
exports.description: What pressing a button does: nudge it down 1px (Kitora), or sink it with an inner shadow (macOS).

exports.name: FOCUS_RINGS
exports.description:
The keyboard-focus indicator: a solid ring (Kitora), a wider, softer halo (macOS), or an accent stroke along the
bottom of a field with no ring (Windows 11). On a toggle (checkbox, radio, switch, slider, toggle) `underline` draws as
`solid`: a stroke under a small control is not a focus indicator.

exports.name: BEVELS
exports.description: A field's edge: flat, a faint inner top shadow that makes it read as recessed (macOS), or the classic sunken bevel (Retro).

exports.name: TABS_STYLES
exports.description: How a tab list draws the selected tab: a raised segment in a track, or a line under it.

exports.name: SURFACES
exports.description: A menu's surface: opaque, or see-through with the page blurred behind it (macOS).

exports.name: HIGHLIGHTS
exports.description: Which colour a highlighted menu item takes: the quiet accent, or the brand colour (macOS).

exports.name: CHECKMARK_SIDES
exports.description: Which side a menu's checkmark sits on.

exports.name: PRESENTATIONS
exports.description: Where a dialog appears: centred, or dropped from the top edge like a macOS sheet.

exports.name: FOOTER_STYLES
exports.description: A dialog footer: a tinted band with a top rule (Kitora), or plain (macOS).

exports.name: MOTION_STYLES
exports.description:
How popups and dialogs move: Kitora's quick fade and zoom (`subtle`), no entrance or exit movement (`none`), or a slower
entrance that overshoots a little (`spring`; sliding panels and toasts only take a little longer, without the overshoot). A dialog presented as a sheet slides from the top edge (unless `none`) and eases
out without overshoot. `prefers-reduced-motion` turns these animations off in every language.

exports.name: FONT_FAMILIES
exports.description: Which font family the language sets: the theme's brand face, the OS's own, Windows' own (Segoe UI Variable first), or a monospace.

exports.name: TOOLTIP_STYLES
exports.description: A tooltip's colours: inverted (the foreground colour with page-coloured text, Kitora), or a small popover-coloured panel with a hairline edge (macOS).

exports.name: SEGMENT_STYLES
exports.description:
A joined toggle group (no spacing between its items): items butted together with only the ends rounded (Kitora),
or a segmented control, a filled track with every segment rounded inside it (macOS).

exports.name: BAR_ENDS
exports.description: How the ends of a progress or meter bar are drawn: rounded (Kitora), or square (Retro, Terminal).

exports.name: BAR_HIGHLIGHTS
exports.description: What a menu bar title takes under the pointer or while its menu is open: the quiet muted fill (Kitora), the accent, or the brand colour with its foreground (Retro).

exports.name: TOOLBAR_PRESSED_STYLES
exports.description: A pressed toolbar button: a brand tint with brand text (Kitora), a muted fill, or pressed into the classic sunken bevel (Retro).

exports.name: AVATAR_SHAPES
exports.description: An avatar's outline: a circle (Kitora), a rounded square that scales with the avatar (a quarter of its side), or a square (Retro).

exports.name: CALENDAR_SELECTED_SHAPES
exports.description: A selected calendar day's outline: a circle (macOS, Material), a square (Retro, Terminal), or rounded by the slot's `cellCorner` (Kitora).

exports.name: CALENDAR_TODAY_STYLES
exports.description:
How a calendar marks today: a ring in the selected colour (Material), a dot under the number, a bolder number in the text colour, or the
number in the brand colour, semibold (`accent`, Kitora). A selected today takes the selected fill and keeps only its dot.

exports.name: CALENDAR_RANGE_BANDS
exports.description:
How the days inside a range are joined: one band across the row with the ends cornered by `cellCorner` (Kitora), a band with fully
round ends (a pill, macOS and Material), or no band at all, each day tinted on its own shape (Retro, Terminal).

exports.name: CALENDAR_WEEKDAY_CASES
exports.description: The weekday header's letters: as the locale writes them (`title`, "Mo Tu"), or in capitals ("MO TU").

exports.name: CALENDAR_HEADERS
exports.description: The caption row: the month centred between the arrows (Kitora), or at the start with both arrows grouped at the end (macOS, Material).

exports.name: SHADOW_SCALES
exports.description:
The shadow scale every part without a slot of its own wears (Tailwind's `shadow-xs` … `shadow-2xl`, which a host routes through
`--dk-base-shadow-*`): the page's own scale (`host`, Kitora), a hairline edge under a soft drop (`crisp`: macOS, Windows 11,
GNOME), Material's key-plus-ambient elevation levels (`tonal`), the classic 3D bevel, framed from `md` up (`bevel`: Retro), or no
shadow at all (`flat`: Terminal).

exports.name: KIT_FOLLOWS
exports.description:
Whether the kits' own versions of a ui part follow its slot: `kit` leaves them their own look (the data grid's rules
and hover, the upload kit's cards), `slot` gives them this slot's values. Kitora's language uses `kit`, so the kits
look exactly as they do with no language; a language without the field loads as `kit`.

exports.name: KitFollow
exports.description: One of {@link KIT_FOLLOWS}.

exports.name: LIST_SELECTIONS
exports.description:
How a selected row in a list or tree is drawn: each list's own look (`kit`, kitora: a tree's brand tint, a task row's lighter one),
a brand tint under the text colour (`tint`), a neutral grey fill (`neutral`, Windows 11), the brand colour with its foreground (`solid`,
a macOS source list, Retro's navy), or inverse video (`inverse`, Terminal). A row that carries its own coloured parts (a task row's
status pills) takes a soft version of `solid` and `inverse`, so its parts keep their contrast.

exports.name: CHIP_SHAPES
exports.description: A chip's outline (a tag, a filter chip, a token in a tags input, a status pill): each kit's own corner (`kit`, Kitora), a capsule (`pill`: macOS, GNOME), or square (Retro, Terminal).

exports.name: KEY_STYLES
exports.description: A keyboard key cap (`Kbd`): each kit's own (`kit`, kitora: a hairline bottom edge), flat, raised off the page, or the classic bevel (Retro).

exports.name: CHIP_TONE_TEXTS
exports.description:
The text of a tinted status pill (a `StatusBadge`'s soft and outline variants): the tone's own colour (`kit`), or the text colour, the
dot and the tint keeping the tone (`ink`: Retro, whose grey face leaves the tone colours under 4.5:1).

exports.name: BUBBLE_SHAPES
exports.description:
A message bubble's outline (ui `Bubble`, the ai-chat and chat kits' messages): Kitora's own corner (`kit`, the page's `2xl` radius, so it
follows the base slot: Windows 11 and Material draw it in their own base corner), a rounder one (`round`, 18px: macOS Messages, GNOME), or
square (`square`: Retro, Terminal; the tail is square too).

exports.name: BUBBLE_TAILS
exports.description:
The tail: the corner on the sender's side. Kitora's (`kit`, tighter, the page's `md` radius), none (`none`, all four corners alike), or a
gentler one (`soft`, half the bubble's corner).

exports.name: BUBBLE_OWN_FILLS
exports.description:
The fill of one's own bubble (a default bubble on the inline end): the bubble's own fill (`kit`, Kitora's muted grey), the brand colour with
its foreground (`primary`: macOS Messages, GNOME), a brand tint (`tinted`: Windows 11, Material), or the muted fill (`muted`).

exports.name: CODE_PALETTES
exports.description:
The colours of highlighted code: Kitora's own token colours (`kit`), or a palette after a platform's editor (`xcode` for macOS,
`vscode` for Windows 11, `material`, `adwaita` for GNOME, `retro`, `terminal`) or GitHub's (`github`). Each is a light and a dark set,
fitted to 4.5:1 on its own language's surfaces; the colours live in the DOM adapter, keyed by this name.

exports.name: CODE_COMMENT_STYLES

The base: the look of every part that has no slot of its own (the kits' panels, rows, chips and windows, and every hard-coded
`rounded-*` and `shadow-*` class). It works through the page's own scales rather than per component: `radius` sets the base radius
every `rounded-*` class is a multiple of, and `shadows` swaps the whole shadow scale. `{ scale: 1 }` with `host` (Kitora)
keeps the page's own radius and shadows, so nothing changes.

props.name: radius
props.description: The base radius (`--radius`): `{ scale: k }` is k times the page's own, `{ px }` a fixed one (0 squares every corner), `{ radius }` the page's own at that step.

props.description: The corner every slot naming `{ role: "control" }` gets: the input-like controls and buttons, at every size, so controls of one height always match.

props.name: surface
props.description: The corner every slot naming `{ role: "surface" }` gets: cards, popovers, menus, dialogs and the other floating or framed panels.

props.name: shadows

exports.name: SLOT_IDS
exports.description: The slot ids, in a stable order (adapters and guards iterate this list).

exports.name: SlotId
exports.description: One slot id, a key of {@link LanguageSlots}.

exports.name: LanguageTokens
exports.description:
Where a language's colours come from.
- `host`: keep the page's own tokens (src/styles.css, a ThemeProvider theme, a theme lab). This is how
  the default language changes nothing for anyone who does not switch.
- `generated`: a theme built by {@link buildTheme } from a seed (so every text pair is contrast-checked),
  with optional per-token overrides per scheme, passed to buildTheme as its overrides: a surface or text
  token is used as given and the fills are fitted against it; a `primary` or `destructive` override is the
  fill's seed. Labels and the ring are taken as given, not re-checked.

exports.name: LanguageTypography
exports.description: A language's typography.

exports.name: DesignLanguage
exports.description: A complete design language.

exports.name: LanguageProblem
exports.description: One problem with a language, as `path: message` (e.g. `slots.button.heights.md: expected a positive number`).

exports.name: FieldSpec
exports.description:
What a slot field holds, as data an editor can draw a control from (the customizer builds its form from these):
a length in px, an amount from 0 to 1, a blur in px (0 allowed), a font weight, a yes/no, one of a closed list, a corner,
a paint, a value per scheme, or a value per control size.

exports.name: isRecord
exports.description: A non-null, non-array object (what JSON objects parse to).

exports.name: RADIUS_NAMES
exports.description: The radius steps a corner may name, smallest first.

exports.name: SLOT_SCHEMA
exports.description:
Every field each slot must carry, with its check. This table IS the slot schema at runtime: a
language read from JSON (an imported or browser-saved theme) is checked against it before use, and the
guard test checks every registered language with it. `satisfies` ties it to the TypeScript types, so a
field added to a slot interface without a check here fails to compile.

exports.name: LanguageChoice
exports.description: A language on offer, by id and label: enough for a picker to list it before its data has loaded.

exports.name: LanguageLoader
exports.description: Loads a language's data (typically a dynamic `import()` of its module).

exports.name: LanguageLoaderEntry
exports.description: A language offered through a loader: its id and label up front, its data when {@link LanguageRegistry.load} asks.

exports.name: LanguageRegistry
exports.description:
The languages an app offers. Built-ins and an app's own register the same way; the first registered
one is the default unless `defaultId` says otherwise. A language is offered with its data (`register`)
or through a loader (`registerLoader`): the synchronous reads (`get`, `list`, `fallback`, `resolve`) see
the languages whose data is in, and `load` brings a lazily offered one in. A registry is a plain object
with no hidden state outside it, so two providers (or a test) never share one by accident; a provider
re-reads it when it changes (`subscribe`).

exports.name: LanguageRegistryOptions
exports.description: Options for {@link createLanguageRegistry}.

exports.name: builtinLanguageRegistry
exports.description:
A fresh registry offering the built-ins (Kitora the default): Kitora's data is in it, the six others register
through their loaders and load on `registry.load(id)` (a provider calls it when one is chosen). Register an app's own
on it. For a registry with every built-in's data up front: `createLanguageRegistry(BUILTIN_LANGUAGES)`.

exports.name: tryCompleteLanguage
exports.description:
A language saved before a slot (or a slot field) existed, made whole: every missing slot and every
missing slot field comes from `base` (default Kitora, so a missing field looks as Kitora's does),
as does a size missing from a per-size field (a switch saved before the `lg` size gets the base's `lg`;
each size is checked on its own, so the base's size fits whatever the language's other sizes are),
and the result is validated strictly, so a field that is present but wrong still fails. For languages
from outside the type system (a saved or imported theme, an older release): the adapter and the React
scope use it, so a language written before this batch of slots renders instead of crashing. The
registry stays strict (`register` rejects an incomplete language); complete first when you want it kept.

exports.name: completeLanguage
exports.description: {@link tryCompleteLanguage}, throwing every problem (as `register` does) when the language cannot be made valid.

exports.name: KITORA_LANGUAGE
exports.description:
Kitora's own look, read off the primitives' Tailwind classes (`packages/ui/src/button.tsx` etc.):
every value here equals the fallback the component uses when no language is applied, which is what
keeps the default pixel-identical. Change one only together with the component's fallback.

exports.name: BUILTIN_LANGUAGE_LOADERS
exports.description:
The built-ins after Kitora, each with a loader that imports its module on demand (a chunk of its own in an app's
build). The ids and labels are here so a picker lists them before their data has loaded; a test keeps them equal to
the data's.

exports.name: BUILTIN_LANGUAGE_CHOICES
exports.description:
Every built-in's id and label, default first: what a picker lists and what a saved language may not reuse, without any
data. A literal, not derived from the loaders: a bundler cannot prove a `.map()` pure, so deriving it would keep the
loaders (and their chunks) in every app that imports this module. A test keeps it equal to the data.

exports.name: CompletedLanguage
exports.description: What {@link tryCompleteLanguage} makes of a value: a complete language, or every problem left after filling.

exports.name: GNOME_LANGUAGE
exports.description: GNOME (libadwaita): bold rounded buttons, grey filled entries, 12px popovers and dialogs, linked buttons, the Adwaita switch.

exports.name: MACOS_LANGUAGE
exports.description:
macOS (Sonoma-era AppKit). Colours are generated from a system-style blue, so every text pair is
contrast-checked. The seed is deeper than AppKit's #007AFF (about 4:1 on white): brand-coloured text
on a 10% brand tint (a soft button, a selected nav pill) needs that margin to keep 4.5:1 (axe found
it at 0.6). In dark mode fills are light with dark labels, Kitora's dark-scheme rule. Greys are
neutral (no tint).

exports.name: MATERIAL_LANGUAGE
exports.description: Material 3 (Material You): a baseline purple, pill buttons, filled fields with an active indicator, 28px dialogs, segmented buttons.

exports.name: RETRO_LANGUAGE
exports.description: Retro (Windows 95 / classic Mac): square corners, bevelled buttons and windows, sunken fields and boxes, a navy highlight.

exports.name: TERMINAL_LANGUAGE
exports.description: Terminal / brutalist: a monospace face, square everything, hard full-strength edges, no shadows, a green accent.

exports.name: WINDOWS_LANGUAGE
exports.description:
Windows 11 (Fluent 2, WinUI 3). Colours are generated from Windows' default accent blue (#0067C0), so every text pair is
contrast-checked; greys are neutral. Segoe UI Variable, 32px controls with a 4px corner, fields with a 2px accent stroke
along the bottom on focus and no ring, Mica-like translucent menus and flyouts, centred dialogs with a grey footer band,
an underlined tab strip (the WinUI pivot), a 40x20 toggle switch with an outlined off state, 20px checkboxes and radios.

exports.name: BUILTIN_LANGUAGES
exports.description: The built-ins with their data, default first (a registry with all of them up front: `createLanguageRegistry(BUILTIN_LANGUAGES)`).
