exports.name: isThemeMode
exports.description: Whether `value` is a {@link ThemeMode}; use it to read a stored or untrusted choice.

exports.name: localThemeStorage
exports.description: `localStorage`, tolerant of private windows and SSR (reads `null`, writes nothing).

exports.name: memoryThemeStorage
exports.description: In-memory storage for tests, previews and SSR.

exports.name: mediaSchemeSource
exports.description: `prefers-color-scheme` via `matchMedia`; light where there is no window (SSR).

exports.name: fixedSchemeSource
exports.description: A scheme source that never changes (tests, screenshots, a forced preview).

exports.name: themeInitScript
exports.description:
A dependency-free script for a raw `<script>` at the top of `<head>` that puts the stored mode, density and design
language on `<html>` before the first paint, as the `ThemeProvider` with the same options would (the `dark` class,
`color-scheme`, `data-theme`, `data-density`, `data-language`): a user who chose dark sees no white first frame on a
hard load. Built from the provider's own storage keys, mode names and "system" query, so the two cannot drift.
Storage that throws (a private window, blocked cookies) leaves the defaults.

exports.name: classSchemeSource
exports.description:
The scheme the page SHOWS, read from the `dark` class on an element (`<html>` by default) and
watched with a MutationObserver, so a toggle from any source (this kit's provider, next-themes, a
hand-written script) is seen live. `light` with no document (a server render).

exports.name: applyThemeToElement
exports.description:
Puts a theme on an element (usually `<html>`): the `dark` class, `color-scheme`, `data-theme` and
`data-density`, and the generated stylesheet in one owned `<style>`. Returns an undo for the style.

exports.name: readTokens
exports.description: The live value of each named custom property on `el` (`--primary` → colour), unparsable ones skipped.
exports.signature: (el: Element, names: readonly string[]) => ReadonlyMap<string, Oklch>

exports.name: browserExportActions
exports.description: The browser default: `navigator.clipboard` and an `<a download>` click on a Blob URL.

exports.name: readDirection
exports.description: The `dir` that applies to `el`: its own or the nearest ancestor's attribute, else `ltr`.

exports.name: applyDirection
exports.description: Sets `dir` on `el` and returns a function that puts the previous attribute back (or removes it).

exports.name: observeDirection
exports.description: Calls `onChange` whenever a `dir` attribute changes anywhere under `root`; returns the unsubscribe.

exports.name: THEME_MODES
exports.description: The modes a user picks; `system` follows the OS.

exports.name: ThemeMode
exports.description: A mode a user picks: `light`, `dark` or `system`.

exports.name: ThemeStorage
exports.description: Where a preference is kept. Synchronous so the first render already has it.

exports.name: SchemeSource
exports.description: Where the OS colour scheme comes from.

exports.name: DARK_CLASS
exports.description: The class src/styles.css keys dark tokens and the `dark:` variant on.

exports.name: DEFAULT_STORAGE_KEY
exports.description: The storage key prefix the providers use unless given one.

exports.name: MODE_SUFFIX
exports.description: Storage suffix (after the provider's `storageKey`) of the mode: `light`, `dark` or `system`.

exports.name: DENSITY_SUFFIX
exports.description: Storage suffix (after the provider's `storageKey`) of the density.

exports.name: LANGUAGE_SUFFIX
exports.description: Storage suffix (after the provider's `storageKey`) of the design language's id.

exports.name: ThemeInitScriptOptions
exports.description: What {@link themeInitScript} reads; the same options the `ThemeProvider` takes, with its defaults.

exports.name: AppliedTheme
exports.description: What {@link applyThemeToElement} writes.

exports.name: ROOT_STYLE_ID
exports.description: Id of the `<style>` element {@link applyThemeToElement} owns in `document.head`.

exports.name: ExportActions
exports.description:
What the designer's Export part does with generated text: copy it and save it as a file. A seam so a
host can route exports elsewhere (a VS Code webview message, a server upload, a Figma plugin bridge)
instead of the browser's clipboard and a download link.

exports.name: slotDeclarations
exports.description: The slot variables of a language for one scheme (every one, always, so a nested scope resets its parent's).

exports.name: baseDeclarations
exports.description:
The base slot for one target: the radius, and the shadow scale as `--dk-base-shadow-<step>`. The page's own scale (`host`) writes
nothing at the root (src/styles.css's fallbacks are its scale), and in a scope clears an outer language's (`initial` makes `var()`
take its fallback again).

exports.name: languageColors
exports.description: A generated language's colour tokens for both schemes (overrides on top of the contrast-checked theme).
exports.signature: (language: DesignLanguage) => { readonly [S in Scheme]: ColorTokens; } | null

exports.name: languageDeclarations
exports.description: Everything a language sets for one scheme at one target: slot variables, colours, and (once, in light, inherited by dark) the font and the base slot.
exports.signature: (language: DesignLanguage, scheme: Scheme, target: LanguageTarget) => readonly Declaration[]

exports.name: languageSelectors
exports.description:
The selectors for a language: the element that carries its colours and font, and the element plus
every boundary below it that carries its slot variables, per scheme. At the root the variables go
on <body>, not <html>: a host may set tokens inline on <html> (a theme lab does), and inline styles
beat any stylesheet, while a value on body wins by being closer (portals mount in body too).
exports.signature: (id: string) => { readonly [T in LanguageTarget]: { readonly [S in Scheme]: string; }; }

exports.name: languageCss
exports.description:
One stylesheet for every language given: the host captures plus, per language and target (in its
layer), the colours and font on the language's element and the slot variables there and on every
{@link LANGUAGE_BOUNDARY} below it, light then dark. Install it once (the React layer renders it
inline, so it is in the server HTML); then `data-language` on <html> or on any element picks the
language below it.

exports.name: applyLanguageToElement
exports.description: Sets `data-language` on `el` (usually <html>) and returns a function that puts the previous value back.

exports.name: languageCssRecord
exports.description: The stored copy of a language's stylesheet ({@link LANGUAGE_CSS_SUFFIX}).

exports.name: languageBootScript
exports.description:
A tiny script for the document <head> that sets `data-language` from storage before first paint, so
a reload in a non-default language does not flash the default first. The server HTML carries the default
language's stylesheet only, so the script also installs the stored copy of the chosen language's stylesheet
(`storageKey` + {@link LANGUAGE_CSS_SUFFIX}) when it is for the same language.

exports.name: LANGUAGE_ATTRIBUTE
exports.description: The attribute that names the active language, on <html> or on a scope element.

exports.name: SLOT_VAR_PREFIX
exports.description: Prefix of every slot variable (`--dk-button-h-md`). Components name these; the guard test pins both sides.

exports.name: LANGUAGE_STYLE_ID
exports.description: Id of the `<style>` a host installs with {@link languageCss} (the React layer renders it inline).

exports.name: Declaration
exports.description: One CSS declaration, `[property, value]` (a custom property or a plain one such as `font-family`).

exports.name: TRANSLUCENT_PANEL_OPACITY
exports.description:
How opaque a translucent panel (menu, popover, sheet) is, per scheme: the least see-through value that keeps body
and muted text at 4.5:1 with the page's darkest or lightest colour right behind it (before the blur, which only
evens it out). A dark panel needs more: a light page area behind it lifts the panel toward its own text colour.

exports.name: LanguageTarget
exports.description: Where a block of declarations lands: `<body>` under a root `data-language`, or a scope element.

exports.name: BASE_SHADOW_STEPS
exports.description: The Tailwind shadow steps a host routes through `--dk-base-shadow-<step>` (src/styles.css: `--shadow-sm: var(--dk-base-shadow-sm, <its own>)`).

exports.name: BaseShadowStep
exports.description: One Tailwind shadow step, `xs` … `2xl`.

exports.name: LANGUAGE_BOUNDARY
exports.description:
Where a scheme or a theme can change below a language: a `dark` / `light` class or a ThemeScope. A
custom property's `var()` is resolved on the element that declares it, so `--dk-tabs-selected:
var(--background)` declared on <body> would carry body's background into a dark-pinned subtree. Slot
variables are therefore declared again on every boundary, where they resolve against that subtree's
own tokens, radius and spacing.

exports.name: LANGUAGE_LAYERS
exports.description:
Cascade layers for the two targets, scope after root: a scope always sits inside the root, so the
later layer makes the nearest language win whatever the selectors' specificity. Appended after
Tailwind's layers; nothing unlayered declares these variables.

exports.name: LANGUAGE_CSS_SUFFIX
exports.description:
Suffix (after the language's storage key) of the stored copy of the active language's stylesheet: `<id>` + newline +
its {@link languageCss}. The providers write it when the language settles; {@link languageBootScript} installs it before
first paint, because the server HTML carries only the default language's stylesheet.

exports.name: LANGUAGE_BOOT_STYLE_ID
exports.description: Id of the `<style>` the boot script installs from that copy; the provider removes it once its own stylesheet is in.

exports.name: CODE_COLOR_KINDS
exports.description: The code token kinds a palette colours (the display kit's `TokenKind` less `plain` and `variable`, which take the text colour).

exports.name: CodeColorKind
exports.description: One of {@link CODE_COLOR_KINDS}.

exports.name: CodeColors
exports.description: One scheme's colours: a CSS colour per kind.

exports.name: CODE_PALETTE_COLORS
exports.description: Every palette but `kit` (Kitora's own colours, which the readers keep as their fallbacks).

exports.name: useControllable
exports.description: One value that is controlled when `value` is given and owned here otherwise.
exports.signature: <T>(value: T | undefined, defaultValue: T, onChange?: (next: T) => void) => readonly [T, (next: T) => void]

exports.name: useSystemScheme
exports.description: The OS scheme from a source, live. Renders `light` on the server and on the first client pass.

exports.name: useDocumentScheme
exports.description:
The scheme the document shows (the `dark` class on `<html>`), live, whoever set it. For a widget
that must match the page without sitting under a ThemeProvider. `light` on the server and while
